title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: k is a base ring, and for a k-module M, V(M) is the functor A ↦ Hom_k(M, A) on k-algebras. It is represented by Spec Sym(M) and is contravariant in M. W(M): A ↦ M⊗A (introduced on the next page) is its covariant companion; both are SGA3/EGA-style notation.

The previous page proved a Yoneda-type statement. Since V(N)×V(N') = V(N⊕N') is represented by Sym(N⊕N'), a natural transformation V(N)×V(N') → V(M) is a map M → Sym(N⊕N'). It is bilinear exactly when it lands in the bidegree-(1,1) part N⊗N'.

This page specialises to M = N = N'. A bilinear composition law on V(M) is the same thing as a k-linear map Δ: M → M⊗M (the 'diagonal'). One calls M a coalgebra, and declares Δ coassociative, cocommutative or counital exactly when the induced law on V(M) is associative, commutative or unital; written out, these are the usual diagrams.

For units: a unit e ∈ V(M)(k) = Hom(M, k) is a counit ε: M → k, unique if it exists. Dually, a linear map V(M) → O_k = V(k) is a map k → M, i.e. an element g of M. It is multiplicative (an 'augmentation' of the algebra object V(M)) iff Δg = g⊗g, i.e. g is group-like; the page reuses the letter e for this element.

Finally, the formula V(lim→ M_i) = lim← V(M_i) holds for arbitrary index categories. It shows that a limit of the algebra objects V(M_i), i.e. a colimit of the coalgebras M_i, is again a coalgebra, and that the associativity, unit and commutativity axioms pass to the limit.

Purpose: this is foundational linear algebra, presenting algebraic structures on vector-group functors as coalgebra structures on modules. It prepares graded modules as actions of diagonalizable groups D(Z) (next page), and presumably the divided-power / Cartier-duality machinery needed for the divided-power de Rham complex of the 1976 IHÉS talk.
errors: The page says 'une lim. proj. de coalgèbres est une coalgèbre'. The formula actually written is V(lim→ M_i) = lim← V(M_i), so what it proves is that an inductive limit (colimit) of coalgebras is a coalgebra, since colimits of coalgebras are created in modules. Projective limits of coalgebras are not computed naively in modules. Either 'proj.' refers to the V side, or it is a slip.
Terminology: the counit ε: M → k is also called a 'coaugmentation', whereas standard usage reserves 'coaugmentation' for k → M. This is minor and not a mathematical error.
Minor point: the letter e is reused for the group-like element g ∈ M after being used for the unit of V(M).

ideas.what: Bilinear maps V(N)×V(N') → V(M) correspond to linear maps M → N⊗N'; hence a coalgebra structure on M is the same as an algebra-object structure on the vector-group functor V(M)
ideas.modern_name: Yoneda/representability description of coalgebras; linear duality between coalgebras and algebra functors (Cartier/Dieudonné style)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Dieudonné, Cartier; Demazure–Gabriel; SGA3 Exp. I)
ideas.where_published: Closely related material on V(M)/W(M) and representability appears in EGA II and SGA3 Exp. I; exact statement unsure

ideas.what: Counit ↔ unit of V(M); group-like elements ↔ multiplicative maps V(M) → O_k
ideas.modern_name: Counit; group-like elements as characters of the dual algebra
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard Hopf algebra theory (Hopf, Milnor–Moore, Sweedler)
ideas.where_published: Analogous statements for diagonalizable groups and characters in SGA3

ideas.what: V(colim M_i) = lim V(M_i), so colimits of coalgebras are coalgebras and the axioms are preserved
ideas.modern_name: Forgetful functor from coalgebras creates colimits

deep.surprise_reason: This is entirely standard expository linear algebra (coalgebras as dual to algebra structures on vector-group functors), written as preliminaries for a divided-power de Rham lecture. Nothing on the page is new.
transcription_corrections: Line 4 likely reads '(appelée aussi "application diagonale")' and refers to Δ, with 'on dit que M devient une coalgèbre' inserted above it.
'lim' on the left side of the formula is the inductive limit lim→ M_i (no arrow is visible); the right side is lim← V(M_i), as transcribed.
'(pour cat. d'indices quelc.)': the struck word is 'cat', replaced by 'd' in the original, so read roughly 'pour d[iagrammes]/cat. d'indices quelconques'.
The illegible phrase after 'k → M' is likely 'on en dit un élément diagonal [group-like] de M (application unité)'; not certain.
'qui le définissent de façon unique' likely means the counit, if it exists, is uniquely determined.
